subtype: Approach: pursuing the desire while ignoring the family [Pitfall]
passage: Day 3 of camp, 10 pm. I still can't believe I'm here. Today my team's line-following car finally stayed on the track and everyone cheered. I've told nobody at home; Mummy thinks I'm at my cousin Lokesh's, doing project work. It felt like freedom all morning. Then at lunch a text came from Lokesh: “Your mom has asked me three times where you are. I said I don't know. Don't do this to me.” Papa rang my phone twice and I let it ring. Someone also told me the shop turned away two big orders because nobody was at the counter. The car works fine. My stomach doesn't. I wanted this so badly that I never looked at anyone else. — Gargi

qa.q: What finally worked for Gargi's team on day three?
qa.a: Their line-following car finally stayed on the track.

qa.q: What is Gargi feeling at the end of the entry?
qa.a: Uneasy and guilty: Gargi's stomach is unsettled because the wanting was so strong that nobody else was considered.

qa.q: What could Gargi have done differently, and why?
qa.a: Gargi could have talked to the parents about the camp and the shop beforehand, because being open lets the family share the plan and keeps their trust.

qa.q: How might Lokesh feel about being asked where Gargi is?
qa.a: Lokesh is put in an awkward spot, asked to cover for something that Lokesh knew little about, which is why the text begs Gargi not to do this.

grounding: A student joins the camp secretly, ignoring the family's need, which breaks trust and leaves the shop uncovered.
